Definition: Dedan, the name of two Cushites and of their territory
BiblicalUsage: Dedan is the name of two Cushites and of the territory their people held, on the trading roads of Arabia. The merchants of Dedan trade in ivory and ebony and precious cloth, and the prophets warn them to flee from the sword. The territory is named with the nations that will fall in the day of the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Dedan shows that no trading nation is outside God's judgment: the caravans and the markets are His, and the merchants answer to Him.
